borne-over.label: Borne over
borne-over.gloss: The verb is motion: a spirit carried above the water (LXX ἐπεφέρετο, Vulgate ferebatur).

wind.label: A wind
wind.gloss: Ruach is weather, not a person; Onkelos keeps God at a remove.

spirit-of-mercy.label: Spirit of mercy
spirit-of-mercy.gloss: A divine disposition blowing over the waters (Palestinian targums).

messiah.label: Spirit of the Messiah
messiah.gloss: Resh Lakish: the ruach of Isa 11:2, brought by repentance-as-water.

bird-hovering.label: Dove hovering, not touching
bird-hovering.gloss: Ben Zoma and Rashi: the bird measures a gap; it does not land.

fluttering.label: Fluttering
fluttering.gloss: Abelard's report of the Hebrew: volitabat, as the eagle of Deut 32:11.

brooding-warmth.label: Bird brooding, warming
brooding-warmth.gloss: Jerome from the Hebrew, Basil's Syrian, then the Latin schools: the Spirit quickens matter like a hen on eggs.

power-not-place.label: Power, not place
power-not-place.gloss: Augustine: 'above' means sovereignty, not position; the Manichees misread it.

craftsman.label: The craftsman's will
craftsman.gloss: The Spirit over the waters as the maker's intention over the wood.

love-gift.label: Love, gift, weight
love-gift.gloss: Confessions XIII: why the Spirit alone is said to be above; pondus meum amor meus.

trinity.label: The Trinity named
trinity.gloss: The verse completes Father (in principio), Son (principium), Spirit.

heart.label: Over the heart
heart.gloss: Isidore's moral reading: the waters are our fluid, dark heart.

throne.label: Throne of Glory
throne.gloss: Rashi: the throne stands in the air, held by the breath of God's mouth.

unus-cardinal.label: The versions keep the cardinal
unus-cardinal.gloss: ἡμέρα μία, dies unus, yoma chad: 'one', not 'first', in every ancient version.

unus-grammatical.label: 'First' needs a second
unus-grammatical.gloss: The series 'one, second, third' is improper (Bereshit Rabbah); or, first and second are relatives and there was no second yet (Bruno).

unus-alone.label: God was alone that day
unus-alone.gloss: Yachid in his world: no angels were made on the first day, so there was no second anything (Bereshit Rabbah, Rashi).

unus-yom-kippur.label: The one day given to Israel
unus-yom-kippur.gloss: 'One day' is the Day of Atonement, the day the Holy One gave them.

unus-24-hours.label: One circuit, twenty-four hours
unus-24-hours.gloss: Day and night together make one revolution, and the whole is named from the day alone.

unus-repeated.label: The same day repeated
unus-repeated.gloss: There is one day only — the angelic light — presented once for each kind of thing made (Augustine).

unus-all-time.label: One day = all time
unus-all-time.gloss: The word holds the whole span of the ages, or the whole work of the six days (Augustine's set-aside reading; Abelard's own).

unus-angelic-unity.label: The unity of angelic dignity
unus-angelic-unity.gloss: 'One' names the undivided attention of the angelic mind, not a place in a series (Angelomus).

unus-eternal-day.label: The true first day is eternal
unus-eternal-day.gloss: This day is first only by number and order of creation; the day that is first by nature is uncreated light (Rupert).

day-precedes-night.label: Day before night
day-precedes-night.gloss: Evening is the end of a finished day, morning the end of the night; days are counted from morning to morning.

day-follows-night.label: Night before day
day-follows-night.gloss: 'One day' rules that reckoning begins at evening (Ben Zoma, b. Chullin 83a).

night-for-rest.label: Night made for rest
night-for-rest.gloss: Day is for labour and night for rest, so only the day's bounds are counted.

day-is-a-measure.label: The day's measure is a creature
day-is-a-measure.gloss: The measure of day and of night was itself made on day one (b. Chagigah 12a).

evening-is-completion.label: Evening completes a work
evening-is-completion.gloss: Vespera is a work perfected, mane the beginning of the next — the Carolingian formula.

evening-is-self-knowledge.label: Evening and morning knowledge
evening-is-self-knowledge.gloss: The creature known in itself is evening; known in the Word and referred back in praise, morning (Augustine).

evening-moral.label: Evening as sin or temptation
evening-moral.gloss: Evening and morning are the deeds of the wicked and the righteous, or sin and renewal, or temptation and the light of justice.

simul.label: All things made at once
simul.gloss: Creavit omnia simul (Sir 18:1): the days are not successive.

six-days-literal.label: Six real days
six-days-literal.gloss: Created at once in matter, distinguished in form through six successive days (the common doctors, Bonaventure).

principio-temporis.label: In the beginning of time
principio-temporis.gloss: The word dates the making: time began with the world, and there was no before (Onkelos, Bede, Rabanus, Remigius, Hugh).

principio-in-filio.label: In the Son
principio-in-filio.gloss: Principium is a proper name of the Word, on the strength of John 8:25 and Ps 104:24 (Ambrose, Augustine, Isidore, Alcuin, the Glossa, Rupert, Honorius).

principio-first-of-all.label: First of all things
principio-first-of-all.gloss: 'In the beginning' means before everything else that follows — in the beginning of the creatures, or on the first day (Augustine's second reading; Bruno, Abelard).

principio-is-first-creature.label: The first creature is a beginning
principio-is-first-creature.gloss: The first intellectual creature may be called a beginning to the things it heads (Augustine, De Genesi imperfectus).

beginning-is-wisdom.label: In Wisdom
beginning-is-wisdom.gloss: The beginning is Wisdom — which is the Torah on one bench (Prov 8:22, Prov 3:19, Neofiti) and the Son on the other (Ps 104:24).

reshit-is-torah.label: The beginning is the Torah
reshit-is-torah.gloss: Reshit is the Torah, called reshit darko: God looked into it as an architect into his plans and created the world (Bereshit Rabbah, Rashi).

reshit-is-israel.label: For the sake of Israel
reshit-is-israel.gloss: Reshit is Israel, called reshit tevu'ato (Jer 2:3); the world was made for their sake.

reshit-construct.label: 'When God began to create'
reshit-construct.gloss: Bereshit is a construct and the verse a subordinate clause: at the beginning of God's creating (Rashi's plain sense, Ibn Ezra; contested by Ramban).

world-has-a-beginning.label: The world is not eternal
world-has-a-beginning.gloss: The point of saying 'in the beginning' at all is that the world had one, against the philosophers (Ambrose, Remigius, Hugh, Ramban).

bereshit-book-name.label: It is the book's name
bereshit-book-name.gloss: The Hebrews name volumes from their opening words, so bresith is the title of Genesis (Jerome, Wigbod, Angelomus).

six-preceded.label: Six things preceded the world
six-preceded.gloss: Torah and the Throne of Glory were made before it; the patriarchs, Israel, the Temple and the Messiah's name were contemplated (Bereshit Rabbah 1:4).

read-it-twice.label: Say the phrase twice
read-it-twice.gloss: In principio is to be repeated — once in the Son, once at the beginning of time — rather than decided (Comestor).

lux-corporalis.label: A bodily light
lux-corporalis.gloss: A material light made to light material things, standing in the sun's place until the fourth day (Basil, Ambrose, Bede, Hugh, Honorius, Comestor, Bonaventure).

lux-angelica.label: The angelic creation
lux-angelica.gloss: The light is the spiritual creature called 'heaven' in v. 1, made light by turning to its Creator (Augustine, Angelomus, Rupert).

lux-hidden.label: Stored for the righteous
lux-hidden.gloss: Too good for the wicked, it was hidden away and is kept for the righteous in the time to come (Bereshit Rabbah, b. Chagigah, Rashi).

lux-garment.label: From the light of his garment
lux-garment.gloss: God wrapped himself in it like a garment (Ps 104:2); the heavens were stretched out of it (Bereshit Rabbah, Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer).

lux-from-temple.label: From the site of the Temple
lux-from-temple.gloss: The light was created from the place of the sanctuary (Ezek 43:2; Jer 17:12).

lux-becomes-luminaries.label: The luminaries were made from it
lux-becomes-luminaries.gloss: The nature of light was made on day one and hung in the firmament on day four (the sages in b. Chagigah 12a; an unnamed opinion in Augustine).

lux-twilight.label: A light like the dawn
lux-twilight.gloss: Not the sun's brightness but what the sky is before sunrise or after sunset (Remigius, Honorius, Comestor, Hugh).

lux-is-day.label: 'Light' just means day
lux-is-day.gloss: The verse answers itself: he called the light Day, so light here is put for day (Bruno).

lux-is-distinction.label: The distinguishing of the works
lux-is-distinction.gloss: The light is the confused heap becoming distinct and knowable, not a thing at all (Abelard).

fiat-is-instantaneous.label: Speaking is making
fiat-is-instantaneous.gloss: No interval between the command and the thing: the Hebrew says only 'let it be, and it was' (Ambrose, Basil, Angelomus, Abelard).

pair-is-formless-matter.label: Unformed matter
pair-is-formless-matter.gloss: The pair names the matter God had made and not yet given form to (Augustine, Angelomus, Hugh, Comestor).

pair-is-under-water.label: Hidden under the waters
pair-is-under-water.gloss: Invisible because the waters covered it, and because there was neither light nor anyone to see (Basil, Alcuin, Angelomus, Ibn Ezra).

pair-is-unfurnished.label: No seed, no living thing
pair-is-unfurnished.gloss: Empty of shoots and void of animals: a list of what was not there yet (Bede, Remigius, Rupert, Abelard, Hugh, Comestor, the targums).

pair-is-a-name-for-us.label: A name fitted to slow minds
pair-is-a-name-for-us.gloss: Not a description but the most serviceable word for formlessness, since earth and the deep are the least comely things men know (Augustine, Confessions XII).

pair-many-senses.label: More than one true reading
pair-many-senses.gloss: Five readings of the clause are all true and none can be shown to be Moses' own (Augustine, Confessions XII.21).

pair-is-two-things.label: A green line and slimy stones
pair-is-two-things.gloss: Tohu and bohu are two creatures made on the first day: a line encircling the world, and stones sunk in the deep (b. Chagigah 12a, Sefer Yetzirah).

pair-is-matter-and-form.label: Matter and its form
pair-is-matter-and-form.gloss: Tohu is the hyle, which can hold no name; bohu is bo hu, the form it puts on (Ramban).

pair-is-astonishment.label: Astonishment
pair-is-astonishment.gloss: Tohu is what astonishes whoever looks at it — the earth bewildered at her lot, or the reader appalled at the emptiness (Bereshit Rabbah 2:2, Rashi, the Bahir).

pair-is-history.label: The verse tells history
pair-is-history.gloss: The clause is the first term of a periodization: the generations from Adam, the four kingdoms, or the Church before her children (Bereshit Rabbah 2:1, 2:3, 2:4; Bruno).

pair-is-our-flesh.label: The earth of our flesh
pair-is-our-flesh.gloss: The soul before it has taken the form of doctrine (Isidore, Wigbod, Rabanus, Remigius, Bruno).

pair-is-not-of-heaven.label: Said of earth, not of heaven
pair-is-not-of-heaven.gloss: The phrase is withheld from heaven, which was filled with angels as soon as it was made (Bede, the Glossa, Angelomus, Abelard).

heaven-first.label: Heaven first
heaven-first.gloss: Beit Shammai: the word order is the order of the acts, and a king has his throne made before its footstool (Isa 66:1).

earth-first.label: Earth first
earth-first.gloss: Beit Hillel: a builder raises the lower storey first (Amos 9:6), and Gen 2:4 and Ps 102:26 name the earth before the heavens.

both-at-once.label: Both together
both-at-once.gloss: The sages, and R. Shimon ben Yoḥai's stewpot and its lid (Isa 48:13); Ambrose, that the order of naming gives heaven no privilege of the firstborn.

order-of-dignity.label: Named for dignity, not order
order-of-dignity.gloss: Heaven stands first because it is worthier, or because the account is about to turn to the earth (Hugh of St Victor; R. Yoḥanan's creation-and-completion).

created-then-stretched.label: Created in one order, stretched in the other
created-then-stretched.gloss: Resh Lakish: heaven was created first, the earth was stretched out first — so both proof-texts stand.

heaven-earth-is-everything.label: A name for the whole creation
heaven-earth-is-everything.gloss: Two visible words standing for all that God made, given so for the weakness of little ones (Augustine, Alcuin, Angelomus, Comestor).

heaven-is-empyrean.label: The empyrean heaven
heaven-is-empyrean.gloss: Not the visible firmament but a fiery — from brightness, not heat — and intellectual heaven, filled with angels as soon as it was made (Remigius, the Glossa, Comestor).

heaven-earth-four-elements.label: The four elements
heaven-earth-four-elements.gloss: Heaven names fire and air, earth names earth and water; the verse announces the material first principles of bodies (Ambrose, Abelard, Ramban, Comestor).

et-includes.label: The particle includes
et-includes.gloss: Et ha-shamayim brings in the sun, moon and constellations; ve-et ha-aretz the trees, the plants and the Garden of Eden (Bereshit Rabbah 1:14, b. Chagigah 12a, Ramban).

shamayim-is-water.label: Sham mayim — 'there is water'
shamayim-is-water.gloss: The name itself says what heaven is made of: water, or fire and water mingled into the firmament (b. Chagigah 12a).

one-earth-only.label: One earth, and no heaven of heavens here
one-earth-only.gloss: If the heavens of v. 1 were the intelligible heaven, the earth beside it could not be the ground; the seven earths are seven regions of the one (Ibn Ezra; Abelard, from the other end).

whole-then-parts.label: The whole first, then the parts
whole-then-parts.gloss: V. 1 is a heading: Scripture commends everything God made in two words before going through it with 'God said' (Augustine, Angelomus, the Glossa).

de-nihilo.label: Out of nothing
de-nihilo.gloss: God made the world, and the matter of the world, from nothing whatever.

matter-then-formed.label: Matter first, then formed
matter-then-formed.gloss: Formless matter was created first — first in origin, not in time — and everything else made out of it.

matter-is-coeval.label: Matter was already there
matter-is-coeval.gloss: God is a craftsman working on a material he did not make. Reported on both benches, held by neither.

three-principles.label: God, exemplar, matter
three-principles.gloss: The philosophers' three principles without a principle, named as the position to be refuted.

all-of-them-created.label: Of every one of them, creation is written
all-of-them-created.gloss: Each thing the objector calls a pre-existing material has its own verse saying God created it.

bara-is-not-ex-nihilo.label: 'Created' does not mean from nothing
bara-is-not-ex-nihilo.gloss: The verb bara is used of the sea-creatures and of man, who were made from something.

creare-vs-formare.label: Created, not formed
creare-vs-formare.gloss: Scripture keeps two verbs apart: what has no pre-existing matter is created, what is shaped out of matter is formed.

hyle-is-tohu.label: The hyle is tohu
hyle-is-tohu.gloss: The one created thing is a substance without form, which the Greeks call hyle and Scripture calls tohu.

made-from-something-of-god.label: From the light and the snow
made-from-something-of-god.gloss: Heaven from the light of his garment, earth from the snow beneath the Throne of Glory.

craftsman-needs-matter.label: A craftsman needs a material
craftsman-needs-matter.gloss: Wood helps the carpenter, silver the silversmith — the analogy that makes creation from nothing unthinkable.

silence-proves-nothing.label: Scripture's silence proves nothing
silence-proves-nothing.gloss: That Genesis does not say when a thing was made does not make it coeternal with God.

world-from-tohu.label: The world was made out of tohu va-vohu
world-from-tohu.gloss: Said with embarrassment, and only because the verse says it.

tenebrae-privatio.label: Darkness is not a thing
tenebrae-privatio.gloss: Darkness is the absence of light, as silence is the ceasing of voice and nakedness the absence of a garment; Scripture never says God made it (Augustine, Angelomus, Hugh).

tenebrae-creatura.label: God made the darkness too
tenebrae-creatura.gloss: The darkness is a work of God like the light — it is called with the light to bless the Lord in Dan 3, and it is on the rabbinic lists of what was made on the first day (Remigius, the Glossa, Wigbod's pupil; Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer, R. Tanḥuma).

tenebrae-angeli.label: The darkness is the apostate angels
tenebrae-angeli.gloss: The light of day one is the angelic creation and the division is between the holy angels and the unclean (Augustine, City of God XI.19; Angelomus, Hugh, Rupert, Comestor).

tenebrae-peccatores.label: The wicked, or their deeds
tenebrae-peccatores.gloss: The division is moral: the just from sinners (Isidore, Remigius, the Glossa), or the deeds of the righteous from the deeds of the wicked (R. Yanai, R. Abahu).

tenebrae-ignis.label: Darkness names the element of fire
tenebrae-ignis.gloss: 'Darkness' in v. 2 is elemental fire, which is dark; the deep is water and the spirit is air (Ramban).

divisio-loci.label: Divided by place and quality
divisio-loci.gloss: The two were set apart in space and time — light over the upper part of the world, twelve hours above and twelve below, opposite hemispheres in turn (Basil, Bede, Rabanus, Honorius, Comestor; and R. Yoḥanan's two generals, each given his bound).

divisio-nominis.label: The dividing is the naming
divisio-nominis.gloss: There is no separate act of separation: 'and he divided' means by the calling of names (Ibn Ezra; entertained once by Augustine and dropped).

divisio-est-ordinatio.label: He did not make it but ordered it
divisio-est-ordinatio.gloss: God makes the forms and orders the privations, as a singer orders his rests and a painter his shadows, so that even a nothing has its place (Augustine).

divisio-est-judicium.label: The division is a judgement
divisio-est-judicium.gloss: A sentence passed, and irreversible: on the devil and his angels (Rupert, Hugh), or on the just and sinners by foreknowledge (Isidore).

divisio-est-instantanea.label: The division needed no second act
divisio-est-instantanea.gloss: The two were never mixed: by the very fact that light was made, the division followed, as putting on a garment ends nakedness (Augustine, Hugh).

formatum-ab-informi.label: The formed from the unformed
formatum-ab-informi.gloss: The dividing is the distinction of the formed thing from the unformed, of the perfect from the imperfect and the distinct from the confused (Wigbod, Abelard, Honorius).

bonum-approbatio.label: 'He saw' is approval, not discovery
bonum-approbatio.gloss: God did not learn that the light was good: what pleased him to be made pleased him to remain (Alcuin, Comestor), or the seeing is in the thought (Ibn Ezra), or a good work attests itself when seen (Ambrose).

bonum-withheld.label: The approval is deliberately withheld
bonum-withheld.gloss: 'It was good' is not repeated after the division, and the divine name is dropped from the naming of the night, so that the darkness should not be approved along with the light (Augustine, Wigbod; R. Elazar, R. Abahu).

havdala-derived.label: The verse is the source of the havdala rule
havdala-derived.gloss: 'He saw … and he divided' — one does not bless over the lamp until he has used its light (R. Ze'eira of Caesarea).

lux-hivdil-set-aside.label: He set the light aside
lux-hivdil-set-aside.gloss: Va-yavdel means he separated it off — for himself (R. Yehuda bar Simon), or for the righteous in the time to come, like a king setting aside a fine portion for his son (the Rabbis).

one-authority-singular-verb.label: The verb is singular, so one maker
one-authority-singular-verb.gloss: Not vaydaberu but vaydaber, not bare'u but bara — no one may say that two authorities created the world (Bereshit Rabbah 1:7; Ibn Ezra; and, to the opposite end, Abelard).

elohim-is-plural-of-persons.label: Eloim is plural: three persons
elohim-is-plural-of-persons.gloss: El is singular and Eloim plural, showing a diversity of persons each of which is God; the singular verb shows that they are one creator and their works undivided (Abelard).

elohim-is-honorific-plural.label: A plural of honour
elohim-is-honorific-plural.gloss: Every language honours the great with a plural — adonim, be'alim, the king speaking of himself in Arabic — so Elohim is the plural of eloah and means nothing more (Ibn Ezra). This is his account of the NOUN. He refuses the same reading of the plural VERB at Gen 1:26, where Saadia offers it to him: see plural-of-majesty-refused.

elohim-is-plural-of-powers.label: The force of all forces
elohim-is-plural-of-powers.gloss: El hem: the root el is force, and 'they' points to all the other forces, so Elohim is the master of them all — with a secret not disclosed (Ramban).

trinity-in-the-triad.label: Father, Beginning, Spirit
trinity-in-the-triad.gloss: The three persons are named in order across the first two verses: God the Father, the Beginning who is the Son, the Spirit borne over the waters (Augustine, Basil, Ambrose, Bede, Bruno, Honorius, the Glossa).

trinity-in-the-formula.label: The threefold formula of the six days
trinity-in-the-formula.gloss: God said — and it was so — and God made: the testimony is tripled everywhere because the creating Trinity works everywhere (Rupert; considered and refused by Augustine).

trinity-is-brought-to-the-text.label: The rule of faith comes first
trinity-is-brought-to-the-text.gloss: The catholic faith is set out before the exposition begins, because heretics drag Scripture to their own opinion; the doctrine is what the chapter is read under (Augustine, De Genesi ad litteram imperfectus).

spirit-is-holy-spirit.label: The spirit of v. 2 is the Holy Spirit
spirit-is-holy-spirit.gloss: Not the air and not a wind: Scripture reserved the name, and no other spirit is meant but the one who completes the Trinity (Basil, Ambrose).

principium-is-the-son.label: The Beginning is the Son
principium-is-the-son.gloss: 'I am the beginning, who also speak to you' (John 8:25) — though the Father too is a beginning, and not from a beginning (Wigbod, Remigius, Bruno).

not-to-angels.label: Not spoken to the angels
not-to-angels.gloss: Whoever the 'let us' addresses, it is not angels: man was not created by angels, or there would be many creators and not one (Bruno).

word-order-is-modesty.label: God is named after his works
word-order-is-modesty.gloss: A mortal king proclaims his name and builds afterwards; the Holy One made the needs of his world and was named after — bereshit bara, and only then Elohim (R. Yudan in the name of Akilas; Ben Azzai).

word-order-is-dangerous.label: The word order had to be changed
word-order-is-dangerous.gloss: The seventy-two elders wrote 'God created in the beginning' for Ptolemy, so that bereshit could not be read as the subject (b. Megillah 9a).

should-have-begun-at-exodus.label: It should have begun at Exodus 12:2
should-have-begun-at-exodus.gloss: The Torah is Israel's law book and ought to have opened with the first commandment given to Israel; the creation account has to be accounted for (R. Isaac, in Rashi).

claim-on-the-land.label: Title to the land
claim-on-the-land.gloss: 'He declared to his people the power of his works, to give them the inheritance of the nations' (Ps 111:6) — so that Israel may answer the charge of robbery (Bereshit Rabbah 1:2; Rashi).

do-not-expound-it.label: It may not be expounded
do-not-expound-it.gloss: Not before two, and not the four questions — what is above, what is below, what is before, what is after (m. Chagigah 2:1; Bereshit Rabbah 1:5 and 1:10).

honour-of-the-maker.label: For the honour of the Maker
honour-of-the-maker.gloss: Whoever has no care for the honour of his Maker, it were fitting he had not come into the world; and the concealed matters are not to be published for the expositor's own glory (m. Chagigah 2:1; Rav Huna in the name of Bar Kappara).

the-bet-is-closed.label: The bet is closed behind
the-bet-is-closed.gloss: The world was made with a bet, closed on three sides and open in front: you may ask only from the day of creation onward (R. Yona in the name of R. Levi).

beginning-is-blessing.label: Bet for blessing, not alef for curse
beginning-is-blessing.gloss: Made with the letter of berakhah rather than of arirah, so that the heretics could not say the world was created with a curse (Bereshit Rabbah 1:10).

moses-is-a-witness.label: Moses wrote as a witness
moses-is-a-witness.gloss: Not in the persuasion of human wisdom nor in the counterfeit disputations of philosophy, but in the showing of the Spirit and of power, as a witness of the divine work (Ambrose).

against-the-philosophers.label: Against the philosophers
against-the-philosophers.gloss: Plato's three principles and the atomists' concourse are a spider's web; the divine mind alone contains the origins and causes of things (Ambrose).

against-the-heretics.label: Because the heretics attack it
against-the-heretics.gloss: The Manichees mock the Old Testament before the unlearned, so the first book must be defended, and defended plainly (Augustine).

written-for-the-unlearned.label: In plain speech, for the unlearned
written-for-the-unlearned.gloss: Not with ornate and polished speech but with plain facts — the usual and simple speech the learned also understand (Augustine).

the-work-shows-the-maker.label: The work shows the worker
the-work-shows-the-maker.gloss: The world is a specimen of the divine working: like building and weaving, it shows the craftsman's skill even when the craftsman is silent (Ambrose).

scripture-is-about-restoration.label: Scripture is about restoration
scripture-is-about-restoration.gloss: The matter of all divine Scripture is the works of human restoration, completed not in six days but in six ages (Hugh of St Victor).

foundation-is-for-secular-writings.label: Foundation belongs to secular writings
foundation-is-for-secular-writings.gloss: The works of foundation are the matter of worldly writings; divine Scripture only descends through them on its way to the Incarnation (Hugh of St Victor).

history-is-the-foundation.label: History is the foundation
history-is-the-foundation.gloss: Scripture is a hall with foundation, wall and roof — history, allegory, tropology — and nothing can be built before the foundation is laid (Comestor).

faciamus-is-the-trinity.label: 'Let us make' is the Trinity
faciamus-is-the-trinity.gloss: The formula changes at this one verse — everywhere else 'let it be', here 'let us make' — to intimate a plurality of persons; the singular of v. 27 then gives the unity of the deity (Augustine, Bede, Alcuin, Wigbod, Remigius, the Glossa, Rupert, Abelard, Hugh, Comestor).

faciamus-to-the-son.label: The Father speaks to the Son
faciamus-to-the-son.gloss: Not to himself, since the verb is not 'I shall make', and not to servants: the address is to the Son, who is the image (Basil, Ambrose, Comestor; refused by Augustine, since 'to our image' would then have to be 'to yours').

faciamus-to-the-angels.label: He said it to the angels
faciamus-to-the-angels.gloss: God took counsel with, or spoke to, the ministering angels — stated outright by Pseudo-Jonathan, argued by Rashi and Ibn Ezra, reported as an option by Remigius, taught with a moral by Hugh, printed at Gen 11:7 by the Glossa, and called a Jewish fiction by Basil.

image-of-the-whole-trinity.label: To the image of the Trinity itself
image-of-the-whole-trinity.gloss: Not to the image of the Father alone, or the Son alone, or the Spirit alone — and who would dare separate the Holy Spirit from that plurality? (Augustine, and the Gloss after him).

counsel-with-the-household-above.label: He took counsel with the household above
counsel-with-the-household-above.gloss: Be-mi nimlakh — with the ministering angels, the court that stands to right and left, out of the humility of the Holy One (Bereshit Rabbah 8:3 and 8:8, b. Sanhedrin 38b, Rashi).

consilium-not-senate.label: A soliloquy, not a senate
consilium-not-senate.gloss: The counsel was held inwardly — be-libbo nimlakh, he took counsel with his heart; non tam senatu quam soliloquio — though the rabbinic bench draws from it that no second party was present and the Latin bench that three persons were (R. Ami, Rupert, Abelard).

refutation-beside-the-claim.label: The refutation is beside the opening
refutation-beside-the-claim.gloss: Wherever the verse gives the minim an opening, the answer stands next to it: 'let us make' answered by 'and he created', 'let us go down' by 'and the LORD came down' (R. Simlai, R. Yoḥanan, Rashi).

dignity-of-the-creature.label: The consultative form marks the creature's standing
dignity-of-the-creature.gloss: A rational creature is made with counsel, so that its nobility may be shown — or, on the other bench, so that the great may learn to ask leave of the lesser (Alcuin, Bede, Hugh, Abelard; Bereshit Rabbah 8:8).

plural-of-majesty-refused.label: Not a plural of majesty
plural-of-majesty-refused.gloss: Saadia's reading of na'aseh as royal speech is refused and its proof texts parsed away one by one — 'these witnesses are false witnesses' (Ibn Ezra, against the Gaon, and against his own account of the plural noun at Gen 1:1).

i-and-the-earth.label: I and the earth
i-and-the-earth.gloss: The plural has a second subject and it is the ground: the earth to bring forth the body from its elements, God to give the spirit (Ramban, crediting R. Yosef Kimḥi).

beginning-is-the-intelligible-world.label: The plan in the maker's mind
beginning-is-the-intelligible-world.gloss: The beginning is the intelligible world, which has no place but the Reason of the God who set it in order, as the city planned by an architect has no place but his soul (Philo). The rabbinic bench says the same thing of the Torah as amon.

law-agrees-with-the-cosmos.label: The law and the world agree
law-agrees-with-the-cosmos.gloss: Moses opened with a cosmogony so that the world should be in harmony with the law and the law with the world, and the man who keeps it be a citizen of the world (Philo). The oldest answer on this crux, and the only one that makes the opening a claim about the law rather than about creation.

heaven-earth-are-incorporeal.label: An incorporeal heaven and an invisible earth
heaven-earth-are-incorporeal.gloss: What was made first was not this heaven and this earth but their incorporeal models, along with the idea of air and of void, which the verse calls darkness and abyss (Philo, reported in Latin by Chalcidius).

firmamentum-is-the-corporeal-heaven.label: 'Firmament' names the heaven as body
firmamentum-is-the-corporeal-heaven.gloss: The perceptible heaven is called stereoma precisely because it is corporeal, body being by nature solid and extended in three directions: the name marks it off from the intelligible heaven (Philo).

spirit-is-life-giving.label: Named God's because it gives life
spirit-is-life-giving.gloss: The breath of Gen 1:2 is called God's because breath is the most life-giving thing and God is the cause of life: an argument from what pneuma does, not from who it is (Philo).

lux-intelligibilis.label: An intelligible light, model of the sun
lux-intelligibilis.gloss: The light of the first day is incorporeal and intelligible, the model of the sun and of the stars, and an image of the divine Reason; the visible lights draw their beams from it (Philo).

divisio-prevents-war.label: Separated so they should not be at war
divisio-prevents-war.gloss: Light and darkness are natural enemies; God not only separated them but set borders in the intervals between, so that neighbouring they should not fight for mastery and put disorder inside the ordered world. The borders are evening and morning (Philo).

unus-not-counted-with-the-rest.label: Not counted in with the other days
unus-not-counted-with-the-rest.gloss: Moses does not even call it first, so that it should not be numbered along with the others; he calls it one, having seen in it the nature of the monad (Philo).

unus-monad.label: The monad's solitariness
unus-monad.gloss: It is called one because of the solitariness of the intelligible world, which has a monadic nature: a claim about being alone, not about position in a series (Philo).

evening-morning-are-incorporeal.label: Evening and morning are among the intelligibles
evening-morning-are-incorporeal.gloss: Morning and evening are to be placed in the order of the incorporeal and intelligible things, ideas and measures and types and seals, so the evening of the fifth verse is not a time of day (Philo).

bonum-is-owed-to-the-fathers.label: The answer belongs to the Latin doctors
bonum-is-owed-to-the-fathers.gloss: Not an answer to the crux but a claim about who owns one: the literal exposition Lyra credits to Rashi was found first by our own doctors, and Rabanus and the Master had already given it (Paul of Burgos against Lyra).
